newsitem.title: INDIA: India raises urea fertiliser price by 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: India raises urea fertiliser price by 10 pct.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday increased the price of urea fertiliser by 10 percent with immediate effect, the United News of India (UNI) said.

UNI quoted Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra as telling parliament that the increase was being effected to correct the imbalance in fertiliser use and increase subsidy support on phosphatic and potash fertilisers.
A government spokesman told reporters on Tuesday that the government had decided to raise the price of urea fertiliser by about 10 percent to 3,660 rupees ($102) per tonne.
The current price of urea fertiliser is 3,320 rupees per tonne.
The spokesman had said the price increase would be announced in parliament.

Mishra said the concession or subsidy on di-ammonium phosphate was being increased to 3,750 rupees per tonne from 3,000 rupees. The concession on single super phosphate was being raised by 100 rupees to 600 rupees per tonne.
He said the concession on muriate of potash (MOP) fertiliser will be increased to 2,000 rupees per tonne from 1,500. ($1 = 35.9 rupees)
